After School at Providence Day School
Providence Day School (TK-12) - Charlotte, NC - Parent-Facing Deep Research Report
registration details change yearly - verify with the school before relying on them.
Executive Summary
Providence Day's after-school offering is division-specific: a nationally recognized Extended Day
program for Lower School and a flexible drop-in Clubhouse for Middle School. The Lower School
program's national recognition and child-development framing are its standout features; the Middle
School Clubhouse addresses the harder-to-serve tween window with a supervised, social space.
Strengths
• Nationally recognized Lower School Extended Day with a development-focused, choice-based
approach.
• A dedicated Middle School drop-in model (Clubhouse) - not always offered by peers.
• Year-round continuity via Summer Programs.
Questions to Confirm on a Visit
• Extended Day hours, ratios, and cost; flexibility of scheduling.
• Clubhouse supervision model and hours.
• Options for Upper School students after dismissal.
• Availability of enrichment/club classes vs. care only.
Caveats
Based on PD's public after-school pages (2025-26). Confirm current hours, fees, and eligibility with the
school (see Sources).
Sources & Where to Verify
After School Options: https://www.providenceday.org/admissions/after-school-options
Extended Day (Lower School): https://www.providenceday.org/lower-school/extended-day
Clubhouse (Middle School): https://www.providenceday.org/middle-school/clubhouse
Summer Programs: https://summer.providenceday.org/

Online Enrichment Registration
● Fall Enrichment Registration Opens: Monday, July 20 at 6:00 a.m.
● Click to Register Enrichment Registration
● Classes are filled on a first-come, first-served basis once registration opens. Since programs fill
quickly, we recommend registering promptly at 6:00 a.m. on the day registration begins.
● Fall Enrichment Registration Closes: Sunday, July 26 at 5:00 p.m.
● Confirmation emails will be sent by Monday, July 27
● Registration in the Extended Day Program is required in order to attend enrichment classes.
Please note that the Extended Day Program will have Open Enrollment from August 3 through
August 17 at 5:00 p.m. Failure to register will result in removal from the enrichment program.
● For registration questions, please contact pat.howe@providenceday.org.
Policy Overview
Program Policies & Billing
Extended Day Registration Required
● To participate in Enrichment Programs, students must also be registered for the Extended Day
Program.
● If your student is not currently enrolled in Extended Day, a link to register will be emailed after
your Enrichment registration is confirmed. All students must be registered for Extended Day on
or before the enrollment deadline or they will be removed from the Enrichment class(es).
Billing
● The fees for this semester will be billed through your Blackbaud Tuition Management account.
● If your student attends the first class and then withdraws from the program, a $25 fee will be
billed.
● If your student attends more than one class, you will be billed for the entire session.
Thank you for your understanding — this policy helps us honor our instructor contracts and maintain
program consistency for all students.
Health & Safety / Program Cancellations
● Commitment to Safety
Providence Day School is committed to maintaining a healthy and safe environment for all
students and staff. We are actively monitoring official health guidelines and will continue to take
appropriate precautions to ensure a safe fall program.
● Program Cancellations
It is our full intent to operate Enrichment Programs as scheduled this fall. However, PDS
reserves the right to cancel programs due to unforeseen circumstances or safety concerns.
● Weather-Related Interruptions
If school is closed due to inclement weather or if a session is interrupted by a Perry Weather
lightning alert, no make-up class or refund will be provided for that session.
Offerings
PLEASE NOTE: Students may only participate in ONE enrichment program per day.
Signing up for multiple programs on the same day impacts availability and planning — thanks
for only selecting one!

Amazing Athletes (TK/K)
Get ready to kickstart your child's journey into the world of sports with Amazing Athletes! In this
dynamic program, we'll cover the basics of 10 different sports, focusing on motor skill
development, nutrition, and muscle identification. Each week, we'll explore two thrilling sports,
accompanied by a "superfood" and muscle group, ensuring every class is packed with fun and
energy! Returning students will continue to build new skills and be challenged upon their
return, ensuring growth and progress with each session. Join us as we lay the foundation for a
lifetime of active, healthy habits! Returning students will continue to build new skills and be
challenged upon their return, ensuring growth and progress with each session.
Amazing Athletes (1st-5th)
Calling all young athletes! Join us for an action-packed adventure as we delve into the world of
sports in Amazing Athletes! Each week, we'll focus on mastering the individual skills of a
different sport through exciting drills, games, and relay races. Whether it's soccer, basketball,
or tennis, participants will hone their skills in a safe yet competitive environment, culminating in
thrilling scrimmages. Students will get a better understanding of nutrition and muscle
identification, as this program is designed to mold well-rounded athletes ready to take on any
challenge! Returning students will continue to build new skills and be challenged upon their

Theatre Explorers: Where Imagination Builds Confidence

Verbal confidence – Speaking clearly, sharing ideas, and building vocabulary
Social-emotional growth – Collaboration, empathy, and expressive play

*NEW – What’s New?
Our enrichment program may include new class offerings as well as updates to select returning
favorites. Based on ongoing program evaluation, student engagement, and family feedback, some
classes may feature refreshed formats, expanded focus areas, or enhanced learning
opportunities—while many longtime favorites continue to provide the engaging experience families
know and value.
For information regarding Enrichment Programs, please email
stefanie.nicholson@providenceday.org
Enrichment Day Schedule
What does my child’s Enrichment day look like?
Our team works closely with students to ensure a smooth and supervised transition to and
from enrichment classes.
Transitional Kindergarten & Kindergarten (TK/K)
Students are picked up directly from their classrooms by a Providence Day School Extended
Day Program teacher
They will:
● Be escorted to the Dining Hall
● Enjoy a school-provided nut-free snack
● Have a bathroom break and water bottle refill
● Be walked to their enrichment class by an Extended Day teacher
● Remain supervised throughout the entire enrichment class
● Be escorted to their dismissal location after class
Dismissal options for TK/K:
● Bus
● Carpool
● Extended Day
Grades 1–2
Students are brought to the Dining Hall at dismissal and check in with Extended Day staff.
They will then:
● Enjoy a school-provided nut-free snack
● Have a bathroom break
● Be escorted to enrichment by an Extended Day teacher
● Remain supervised throughout the class
● Be escorted to their dismissal location after class
Dismissal options for Grades 1–2:
● Carpool
● Parent pickup from Extended Day
● Extended Day
Grades 3–5
Students walk independently to the Dining Hall and check in with Extended Day staff.
From there, the schedule is the same:
● Nut-free snack
● Bathroom break
● Escorted to enrichment
● Supervised throughout class
● Escorted to dismissal or Extended Day after class
Dismissal options for Grades 3–5:
● Carpool
● Parent pickup from Extended Day
● Extended Day
Snack Information:
Students do not need to bring a snack. Extended Day provides a nut-free snack each day.
Frequently Asked Questions
Q. Does my child need to be registered for Extended Day to participate in Enrichment?
Yes. Students must be registered with Providence Day School Extended Day Program prior to
the registration deadline.
Q. Will I be billed if my child drops Enrichment?
No fee is charged if your child is withdrawn before the first class.
If your child attends one class, a $25 administrative fee applies.
If your child attends more than one class, the full semester fee applies.
Q. Will I continue to pay for Extended Day after Enrichment ends?
Yes. Extended Day registration remains active for the school year unless changes are
submitted directly to pds.extendedday@providenceday.org
Q. How do I pay my Enrichment bill?
Enrichment fees will appear in your Blackbaud Tuition Management account.
For billing questions, please contact Monique Gelista at monique.gelista@providenceday.org
Q. What happens if school is canceled or dismissed early?
There are no make-up classes or refunds for weather-related school closures or early
dismissals.
Q. How will I know if an outdoor Enrichment is canceled due to weather?
Families will receive an email notification prior to class if weather impacts programming.
Q. What if my child is absent or dismissal plans change?
Please email pds.extendedday@providenceday.org
Q. Will my child receive a snack? Can I send one?
Extended Day provides a nut-free snack daily, so students do not need to bring one.
For dietary questions, please contact our Extended Day nurse, Lisa O’Neal, at
lisa.oneal@providenceday.org
Q. Who should I contact with questions about Enrichment?
Contact the Enrichment Coordinator, Stefanie Nicholson, at
stefanie.nicholson@providenceday.org

After School Pricing at Providence Day School
Providence Day School (TK-12) - Charlotte, NC - After-School Program Pricing (2026-27)
Pricing by Grade & Days per Week
Extended Day serves Lower School students (TK-Grade 5), open 1-6 p.m. on regular school days (Activity Days 7:45 a.m.-6 p.m.). Families register for a weekly schedule of 1-5 days per week; the fee is charged monthly via Blackbaud Tuition Management. There is explicitly no drop-in option for Extended Day. Monthly rates for 2026-27, by grade, time slot, and days per week:

| Grade · time slot (monthly, 2026-27) | 1 day/wk | 2 days/wk | 3 days/wk | 4 days/wk | 5 days/wk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TK · 1-3 pm | $140 | $225 | $315 | $400 | $490 |
| TK · 1-4:30 pm | $165 | $275 | $385 | $500 | $610 |
| TK · 1-6 pm | $190 | $330 | $470 | $610 | $750 |
| K · 2-3 pm | $100 | $145 | $195 | $240 | $290 |
| K · 2-4:30 pm | $130 | $210 | $290 | $370 | $450 |
| K · 2-6 pm | $165 | $275 | $385 | $500 | $610 |
| Grades 1-5 · 3-4:30 pm | $100 | $150 | $195 | $245 | $290 |
| Grades 1-5 · 3-6 pm | $135 | $220 | $300 | $385 | $470 |

Middle School Clubhouse
Clubhouse, the Middle School after-school program, is drop-in: Monday-Friday, 3:10-6:00 p.m., starting the first day of school. Cost is a $100 annual registration fee per student; no per-day or hourly rates are published.
Fees & Fine Print
• Extended Day annual registration fee: $80.
• Late pick-up: $1.00 per minute after 6:00 p.m., charged to the monthly bill.
• Schedule-change adjustment rate: $30/hour (unexpected circumstances; the school distinguishes this from drop-in pricing). Schedule changes must be emailed by the 1st of the month.
• Semester enrichment classes carry a separate, unpublished fee (pro-rated only if a student withdraws after one class).
Notes & Gaps
• The tuition page itself publishes no Extended Day/Clubhouse pricing; it links to the two program pages.
• Full-tier rows (TK 1-6 pm, K 2-6 pm, Grades 1-5 3-6 pm) and the $100/$750 floor/ceiling were re-verified 3-0 against live sources; remaining cells come directly from the official fee document's text export.

After School at Providence Day School
Providence Day School (TK-12) - Charlotte, NC - Program Overview
registration details change yearly - verify with the school before relying on them.
At a Glance
Providence Day offers two main after-school options by division: a nationally recognized Extended
Day Program for Lower School students, and the Middle School Clubhouse, a drop-in space for
Middle Schoolers. Summer Programs round out the year-round options.
The Two Options
• Extended Day (Lower School) - nationally recognized; teachers actively promote each child's
social, emotional, and physical development through nurturing relationships, flexible scheduling, and
choice.
• Clubhouse (Middle School) - open to all Middle School students to drop in, catch up with friends,
study, unwind, play, and eat in a safe, supervised space.
Note
The public pages emphasize Lower and Middle School; families of Upper School students should ask
about supervised study or activity options after dismissal. Hours, fees, and registration are confirmed
with the school.
Sources & Where to Verify
After School Options: https://www.providenceday.org/admissions/after-school-options
Extended Day (Lower School): https://www.providenceday.org/lower-school/extended-day
Clubhouse (Middle School): https://www.providenceday.org/middle-school/clubhouse
Summer Programs: https://summer.providenceday.org/

# Providence Day School — After School Redesign Research (2026)

- Compiled: July 27, 2026, for the After School research-area redesign (four cards:
 Coverage Map, Cost Planner, A Day Inside + Enrichment, Verdict & Visit Checklist).
- Every figure below is transcribed from a Providence Day source. Where the school
 publishes nothing, this file says NOT PUBLISHED rather than estimating.
- The existing `Providence Day - After School - Pricing.md` re-verified 100% clean in
 this pass — all 40 fee cells, both registration fees, the late fee and the adjustment
 rate matched the official fee document exactly. No corrections were needed.

Dismissal times, all divisions (official Daily Schedule PDF):

| Division | Dismissal |
| --- | --- |
| Transitional Kindergarten (TK) | 1:00 pm |
| Kindergarten | 2:00 pm |
| Grades 1–5 | 2:50 pm |
| Middle School | 3:10 pm |
| Upper School | 3:10 pm |

Arrival, all divisions: parents encouraged to arrive 7:30–7:50 am; students enter
classrooms 7:50 am; class begins at 8:00 am. Middle and Upper School share one bell
schedule; only lunch differs (MS 11:55–12:40, US 12:45–1:30).

Programs by division:

| Division | Program | Hours | Covered? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TK | Extended Day | 1:00–6:00 pm, 3 tiers | Yes |
| K | Extended Day | 2:00–6:00 pm, 3 tiers | Yes |
| Grades 1–5 | Extended Day | 3:00–6:00 pm, 2 tiers | Yes |
| Middle School | Clubhouse | 3:10–6:00 pm, M–F, drop-in | Yes |
| Upper School | — | — | NO published program |

Extended Day locations: Auerbach Hall and the Levine Family Extended Day House.
Clubhouse location: modular classrooms in the West Lot, near the Extended Day house.

Pickup tiers and entry price (1 day/week, monthly). NOTE: the app's Coverage Map
surfaces the **5 day/week** column from the full matrix below, not this 1-day
entry column, because full-time is the common case and a 1-day figure reads as
"the price" when it is the cheapest possible one. The full matrix is the source
of both:

| Grade band | Tier | Entry price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TK | 1–3 pm | $140 |
| TK | 1–4:30 pm | $165 |
| TK | 1–6 pm | $190 |
| K | 2–3 pm | $100 |
| K | 2–4:30 pm | $130 |
| K | 2–6 pm | $165 |
| Grades 1–5 | 3–4:30 pm | $100 |
| Grades 1–5 | 3–6 pm | $135 |
| Middle School | 3:10–6 pm (no tiers) | $100/yr flat |

TK and K each get three tiers including a short "wait for a sibling" tier; grades 1–5
get two. The school frames the short tiers around sibling logistics — "many children
wait for an older sibling to get out of school."

Notes & gaps
- Upper School (grades 9–12): NOT PUBLISHED / no program exists. The official After
 School Options page lists exactly two programs, Extended Day and Clubhouse.
- Before-school care: NOT PUBLISHED at any division. Extended Day runs 1–6 pm on
 regular days; morning coverage appears only on Activity Days. The 7:30–7:50 am
 arrival window is unsupervised drop-off, not a care program.
- Activity Days (teacher workdays, parent-teacher conferences, most school holidays):
 Extended Day operates 7:45 am–6 pm, opening at 7 am on parent-teacher conference
 days, with themed activities. Sign-up is mandatory even for enrolled families.
 Activity Day fee: NOT PUBLISHED.
- Discrepancy to flag: grades 1–5 dismiss at 2:50 pm but the fee matrix bills them from
 3:00 pm. The 2:50–3:00 gap is not explained on any published page.
- Summer: "Summer at Providence Day School", https://summer.providenceday.org/ — nine
 sessions, June through early August. Extended Day explicitly does not run in summer
 ("opens on the first day of school and closes on the last day of school"). Summer
 rates, grade ranges and hours: NOT PUBLISHED on the dates-rates page.

| Grade · time slot | 1 day/wk | 2 days/wk | 3 days/wk | 4 days/wk | 5 days/wk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TK · 1–3 pm | $140 | $225 | $315 | $400 | $490 |
| TK · 1–4:30 pm | $165 | $275 | $385 | $500 | $610 |
| TK · 1–6 pm | $190 | $330 | $470 | $610 | $750 |
| K · 2–3 pm | $100 | $145 | $195 | $240 | $290 |
| K · 2–4:30 pm | $130 | $210 | $290 | $370 | $450 |
| K · 2–6 pm | $165 | $275 | $385 | $500 | $610 |
| Grades 1–5 · 3–4:30 pm | $100 | $150 | $195 | $245 | $290 |
| Grades 1–5 · 3–6 pm | $135 | $220 | $300 | $385 | $470 |

Range: $100/mo (K or grades 1–5, short tier, 1 day) to $750/mo (TK, full tier, 5 days).
A full-time working family in grades 1–5 (3–6 pm, 5 days) pays $470/month.

Fees & fine print
- Extended Day annual registration: $80.
- Clubhouse annual registration (Middle School): $100/student.
- Late pickup: $1.00 per minute after 6:00 pm, charged to the monthly bill.
- Schedule-change / adjustment rate: $30/hour, for unexpected circumstances. The school
 explicitly distinguishes this from drop-in pricing.
- Drop-in for Extended Day: none — "No drop-in option" is stated explicitly.
- Enrichment withdrawal: no fee if withdrawn before the first class; $25 administrative
 fee after one class; full semester fee after more than one class.
- Schedule changes must be emailed by the 1st of the month to
 pds.extendedday@providenceday.org.
- Billing: Extended Day fees are charged monthly via Blackbaud Tuition Management.
 Enrichment fees also appear in the Blackbaud account.

Notes & gaps
- Number of Extended Day billing months: NOT PUBLISHED. The fee document gives monthly
 rates but never states how many months are billed.
- Sibling discounts: NOT PUBLISHED, for either tuition or Extended Day.
- Billing-platform ambiguity: the fee doc names Blackbaud, while the tuition/aid pages
 reference Clarity and an archived FAQ references Smart Tuition.
- Financial aid: the Tuition & Financial Assistance page states additional fees apply
 for Extended Day or Clubhouse and that "Financial assistance may be available for
 some of these additional costs" — an explicit, if hedged, statement that aid can
 reach after-school fees. About 21% of families receive some assistance.
- 2026-27 tuition context: TK $25,510 | K $28,010 | Grades 1–5 $32,960 | Grades 6–12
 $36,325.

sections.text:
The enrichment day, in the school's own words (Fall 2026 Enrichment packet, "Enrichment
Day Schedule"). This is a published, division-specific rhythm — not an estimate:

- TK/K — picked up directly from their classrooms by an Extended Day teacher; escorted
 to the Dining Hall; school-provided nut-free snack; bathroom break and water bottle
 refill; walked to the enrichment class by an Extended Day teacher; supervised
 throughout the class; escorted to their dismissal location after class.
 Dismissal options: bus, carpool, Extended Day.
- Grades 1–2 — brought to the Dining Hall at dismissal and check in with Extended Day
 staff; nut-free snack; bathroom break; escorted to enrichment; supervised throughout;
 escorted to dismissal after class.
 Dismissal options: carpool, parent pickup from Extended Day, Extended Day.
- Grades 3–5 — walk independently to the Dining Hall and check in with Extended Day
 staff; from there the schedule is the same.
 Dismissal options: carpool, parent pickup from Extended Day, Extended Day.

Snack: students do not need to bring one — Extended Day provides a nut-free snack daily.

Study hall: grades 3–5, Monday–Thursday, 3:15–4:00 pm — "a quiet space for independent
study hall". Explicitly independent study only, with no one-on-one academic assistance.

The program in the school's own words
- "Teachers actively promote each child's social, emotional, and physical development
 through nurturing relationships, flexible scheduling, and choices that reflect each
 child's individual needs, interests, and abilities."
- The school describes Extended Day as nationally recognized and as providing "an
 enriching experience".
- Director Lynn Mayhew (via Scoop Charlotte, 2016): "It's literally a home away from
 home." / "This truly is their house when they can't be at home."

Middle School Clubhouse, in the school's own words
- "Clubhouse is open to all Middle School students on a drop in basis during after
 school hours."
- "open to all Middle School students to drop in to catch up with friends, study,
 unwind, play and eat"
- Emphasis on "a safe, fun, and inclusive space". Daily nutritious snacks provided.
 Students may self-register and sign themselves in and out for sports practices, games,
 music lessons, theater rehearsals and other approved campus events.

Health and safety (Extended Day)
- All staff trained in CPR, AED and First Aid; registered nurse on duty daily; access to
 student health records via the Magnus system.
- Discipline philosophy: "discipline with dignity".
- Allergy protocol: no peanut or tree nut products served; nurse reviews food content
 for other allergies; home snacks containing nuts prohibited.
- Illness: sick children cared for in a "Get Well Room"; must be fever-free without
 medication for 24 hours before returning.
- Medication: written parental permission required; stored in the locked nurse's office
 with a daily confidential log.

### Fall 2026 enrichment catalog — VERIFIED from the school's packet

All classes run 10 sessions. Fees: $200 for TK/K classes, $220 for grades 1–5 classes.
Students may participate in only ONE enrichment program per day. Registration in the
Extended Day Program is required in order to attend enrichment classes.

Named instructors and providers: Coloring on Canvas LLC (Art); Charlotte Chess Center
and Scholastic Academy (Chess); Charlotte Speech & Hearing Center (YoLa); Mad Science
Charlotte (Science); Ari Patterson (Charger Cheer); Eliza Newell, third-degree black
belt (Karate); Todd Johnson, PDS Middle School Computer Science teacher (Coding); Kris
Jones, PDS Varsity Girls Track and Field Head Coach (Running Club); Terry Tadeo, Tommy
Racano and Paul Burnam (Wrestling).

Registration mechanics (Fall 2026)
- Registration opened Monday, July 20 at 6:00 a.m. and closed Sunday, July 26 at 5:00 p.m.
- Classes fill first-come, first-served; the school recommends registering promptly at
 6:00 a.m. on opening day because "programs fill quickly".
- Confirmation emails sent by Monday, July 27.
- Extended Day Open Enrollment ran August 3 through August 17 at 5:00 p.m.; failure to
 register results in removal from the enrichment program.
- If TK classes do not fill they may be combined with Kindergarten; if grades 3–5
 classes do not fill they may be combined with grades 1–2 at the earlier time slot.
- Weather: if school closes or a session is interrupted by a Perry Weather lightning
 alert, no make-up class or refund is provided.

Notes & gaps
- The website's public enrichment list is a historical/illustrative roster ("past and
 present") covering roughly 28 names — Art, ASL, basketball, Capoeira, cheer, chess,
 dance, finance & investment, Girls on the Run, golf, guitar, karate, lacrosse, Let Me
 Run, OT Fun, piano, science, soccer, tennis, theater, ukulele, volleyball, Wildlife
 Wonders, woodworking, wrestling, yoga, YOLA, Zumba. The Fall 2026 packet above is the
 actual term catalog and supersedes it for this term.
- No cap on how many activities a family may register for, subject to the one-per-day rule.

sections.preview: Strengths - Best-in-class price transparency: a complete published 40-cell (grade × tier × days) matrix in an official document, so a family can compute an exact annual cost before applying. - Three-tier flexibility for the youngest students, explicitly designed around sibling-pickup logistics — the 1:00 pm TK…
sections.text:
Strengths
- Best-in-class price transparency: a complete published 40-cell (grade × tier × days)
 matrix in an official document, so a family can compute an exact annual cost before
 applying.
- Three-tier flexibility for the youngest students, explicitly designed around
 sibling-pickup logistics — the 1:00 pm TK dismissal is a real burden and the school
 priced an answer to it.
- 1–5 days/week at every tier, so part-time families are not forced to buy five days.
- A published, division-specific enrichment day rhythm with escorted transitions and a
 school-provided nut-free snack — unusually concrete operational detail.
- Serious health and safety infrastructure: RN on duty daily, Magnus records
 integration, full CPR/AED/First Aid staff training, nut-free protocol, Get Well Room,
 locked medication log.
- A real 15-class Fall 2026 enrichment catalog with published fees, days, grade bands
 and named outside professional providers.
- Financial assistance may extend to Extended Day and Clubhouse — written on the
 tuition page, and uncommon among peers.
- Strong Activity Day coverage: 7:45 am–6 pm on teacher workdays and most holidays,
 opening at 7 am on conference days — a full working-parent day on exactly the days
 that usually break childcare.
- Clubhouse is cheap and frictionless: $100/year flat, unlimited drop-in, with
 self-sign-out to practices and rehearsals.

Watch-outs
- No Upper School coverage at all — grades 9–12 dismiss at 3:10 pm with nothing published.
- No before-school care at any division on regular days, even though Activity Days show
 the capability exists (7:45 am, or 7 am on conference days).
- No drop-in for Lower School, stated explicitly. Occasional-need families are pushed to
 the $30/hour adjustment rate, which the school says is not drop-in pricing.
- Enrichment is gated behind Extended Day enrollment, so an enrichment class always sits
 on top of a monthly Extended Day charge.
- Activity Day fee is unpublished — an unbudgetable line item on days families most need
 coverage.
- Schedule changes are rigid: email required by the 1st of the month.
- Study hall is thin and narrow — grades 3–5 only, Mon–Thu only, 45 minutes, explicitly
 independent study with no one-on-one help. Grades 1–2 get none.
- Cost stacks on already-high tuition: grades 1–5 full-time is $470/mo on top of
 $32,960; TK full-time is $750/mo on top of $25,510.
- The 2:50 vs 3:00 gap for grades 1–5 (dismissal vs billed Extended Day start) is
 unexplained.
- Late pickup is $1.00/minute and unbounded.
- Billing-platform ambiguity: Blackbaud vs Clarity vs Smart Tuition across sources.
- No summer continuity — Extended Day closes on the last day of school and summer is a
 separate paid program with unpublished rates.
- No published Clubhouse daily structure, staff ratio, or homework-support commitment.

Visit checklist
- What is the Activity Day fee, and is it per-day or bundled for monthly-enrolled families?
- How many months is Extended Day billed — 9, 10, or 12? This changes the annual total
 by hundreds of dollars.
- Is there any Upper School after-school supervision — library, study hall, a supervised
 space — even if not a formal program?
- Is there truly no before-school option? If Activity Days can open at 7:00–7:45 am, why
 not regular days, and is there a demand list?
- What exactly happens between 2:50 and 3:00 pm for grades 1–5, and is it billed?
- How does financial assistance actually apply to Extended Day and Clubhouse — same
 award rate as tuition, and does it reach enrichment fees?
- Which platform actually bills Extended Day — Blackbaud, Clarity, or Smart Tuition?
- Are there sibling discounts on Extended Day or Clubhouse? Two children at $470/mo is
 $940/mo.
- What is the staff-to-child ratio by age group, and what is staff retention?
- Can you change tiers mid-year, and does the $30/hour adjustment rate apply?
- Clubhouse specifics: ratio, homework support, and is the $100 really the only cost?
- Is Extended Day capacity-constrained at any tier, especially 3–6 pm five-day?
- How do enrichment classes interact with the pickup tier — if a class runs to 4:45,
 must you buy the 6 pm tier?
